title: add-cross-run-stability-and-denoise-eval-hook-for-prompt-sets
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a CI hook that runs repeated evals and a denoising resampler to detect unstable prompt-set regressions and surface variance-driven failures in CI; no user-facing API changes.
description: Motivation: CI has historically caught mean-regression but misses flaky or highvariance regressions introduced by model changes, quantization, or runtime scheduling. This PR adds a cross-run stability CI hook that runs a compact prompt-set across multiple randomized seeds and uses a denoising resampling step to detect changes in both central tendency and output variance. The hook introduces a new stability_score metric (combines bootstrap mean delta, inter-run variance ratio, and token-level agreement) and a noise-aware gate that fails CI when the expected mean delta exceeds threshold and stability_score < threshold. Implementation summary: 1) core hook at eval_harness/hooks/cross_run_stability.py that orchestrates N independent runs (default 5) with configurable random seeds, computes per-example bootstrap CIs, and aggregates cohort-level stability_score; 2) denoise resampler module that runs lightweight label-free reruns and builds a consensus output to reduce single-run noise impact; 3) CLI flag --stability-hook in eval-runner to enable locally; 4) unit tests and integration tests under tests/ that simulate synthetic drift and flaky outputs; 5) CI pipeline additions in .github/workflows/eval-ci.yml to run the stability hook on PRs that touch eval-related directories and when a new model is promoted. Operational notes: thresholds are conservative by default (mean delta 1.5% and stability_score 0.7) and live behind a feature flag eval.stability_gate so we can rollout progressively to the repo and to selected projects; there is an opt-out decorator for long-running golden test suites. Backwards compatibility: the hook is additive and not enabled by default for existing repos unless the feature flag is set. Checklist: - [x] Core orchestration and denoising algorithm implemented - [x] Unit tests for resampler and score aggregation - [x] Integration test that fails on synthetic high-variance regression - [x] CI workflow entry and gating rule - [x] Documentation: README for the hook and runbook for triage - [x] Linear tickets linked for rollout and dashboarding How to run locally: pip install -e . then python -m eval_harness.runner --stability-hook --stability-runs 5 --stability-seed-base 1000 Examples and expected output are in tests/fixtures/ and the run prints a short summary table with stability_score, bootstrap mean delta, CI decision and links to artifact logs. Rollout plan: enable behind feature flag for internal e2e job, run in monitoring mode (logs only) for 2 weeks, then enable soft-fail (mark as warning) for 1 week, then gate on merge if no signal drift. Related work: ENG-2031 (prompt regression monitoring), ENG-2089 (eval CI orchestration improvements), SUP-445 was the support ticket that surfaced noisy failure patterns in customer tests. No breaking changes to public APIs. Merge: squash and merge after final reviewer approvals and CI green.
commits_summary: 3 commits: 1) initial cross-run stability hook and stability_score metric; 2) add denoise resampler, CLI flag, and integration tests; 3) fix race in resampler thread pool and tighten default thresholds
review_comments: Arjun Patel: This looks solid overall, one question on the stability_score composition — can we make the weights configurable via config with sensible defaults?
Maya Chen: Good point, added config.default.stability_weights and documented the defaults in docs/hooks/stability_hook.md
Sofia Martinez: The denoising rerun adds infra cost for CI, please add a fallback path that uses a lightweight token-agreement heuristic when budget is constrained.
Maya Chen: Added a budget-aware path in denoise_resampler that switches to token-agreement mode when ci.budget_estimate < threshold; included tests for both paths.
Ben Liu: Minor: the integration test is flaky on mac builders due to random tmp file ordering, please switch to tempfile.TemporaryDirectory to avoid ordering assumptions.
Maya Chen: Fixed the tempfile usage and re-ran CI.
Sofia Martinez: Approved after CI green and docs update.
Release-captain-bot: PR passed CI and is approved by required reviewers.
